page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge within the average performance tier across all tested metrics. In CPU-intensive tasks, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1436.68 and a multi-core score of 30666.35, while Geekbench returned a single-core score of 1287.0 and a multi-core score of 11107.0. Memory performance tests showed a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1705.41 GB/sec, which drops to 109.89 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 48.22 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 21.45 GB/sec and processed 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second. Large language model inference speeds reached 1539.55 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, but decreased to 45.98 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge offers a standard general-purpose hardware profile with dedicated compute resources, avoiding the performance fluctuations associated with shared-core environments. However, the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external storage attachments and limiting its utility for heavy deep learning training or high-IOPS database tasks. The instance is suited for workloads such as multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, Redis caching layers, and moderate database operations that benefit from dedicated high-frequency CPU cores and a balanced memory-to-CPU ratio.
